groups.title: One more thing · Now spend something, and prove it

beats.label: Ask it something easy
beats.cue: [needs-key] “A-1041 is in the notes. The cheap lane reads it, cites it, and the checker passes the draft — no escalation, no strong-model bill.”
beats.script: A-1041 is in the notes. The cheap lane reads it, cites it, and the checker passes the draft — no escalation, no strong-model bill. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work.
beats.command: crewhaus run live/crewhaus.yaml --prompt "Has order A-1041 arrived yet?"

verify.note: single-turn run; needs a model credential. The answer is in notes/orders.md, so the cheap lane's read + grep are enough and the checker should pass the draft on the first grade

beats.label: Ask it something the cheap lane cannot settle
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The refund window lives in bin/refund-window.sh, and the cheap candidate denies Bash. So this is the turn that escalates.”
beats.script: The refund window lives in bin slash refund-window dot sh, and the cheap candidate denies bash. So this is the turn that escalates. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work.
beats.command: crewhaus run live/crewhaus.yaml --prompt "Order A-1043 was delivered on 2026-08-14. Today is 2026-09-07 — is the refund window still open?"

verify.note: single-turn run; needs a model credential. The cheap candidate's permissions deny Bash(**), so the refund verdict cannot come from the fast lane — the checker's sub-threshold grade re-runs the turn on $strong, which may run ./bin/refund-window.sh (OPEN, 24 days)

beats.label: Replay the route, turn by turn
beats.cue: [needs-key] “route explain is a timeline: the decision per turn, and every draft → grade → escalate transition with its model and its cost.”
beats.script: Route explain is a timeline: the decision per turn, and every draft, grade and escalate transition with its model and its cost. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay.
beats.command: crewhaus route explain $(ls -t .crewhaus/sessions/*.jsonl | head -1 | xargs basename | sed 's/.jsonl//')

verify.note: reads the session the previous (needs-key) run beats wrote. Empty without one: route explain replays the durable model_route / model_directive / model_stage lines from .crewhaus/sessions/<id>.jsonl, so a real credentialed run has to come first

beats.label: Measure the two arms instead of guessing
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Same six samples, once per arm. --record gives each arm its OWN baseline lineage, which is what makes the comparison mean anything later.”
beats.script: Same six samples, once per arm. Record gives each arm its own baseline lineage, which is what makes the comparison mean anything later. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call.
beats.command: crewhaus eval live/crewhaus.yaml --dataset eval/dataset.jsonl --graders eval/graders.yaml --models '$fast,$strong' --record --seed 42 -o live/matrix

verify.note: runs 6 samples per arm; needs a model credential. `--models` and `--routing` are mutually exclusive — a matrix already pins one arm per cell. The single quotes matter: an unquoted $fast is expanded away by the shell before the CLI sees it

beats.label: Ask which arm won
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Six samples is below the power floor, so it answers UNDERPOWERED instead of naming a leader. That is the honest answer, and it is the point.”
beats.script: Six samples is below the power floor, so it answers underpowered instead of naming a leader. That is the honest answer, and it is the point. [[pause:1.8s]] This is a live, credentialed step and is intentionally excluded from offline replay.

verify.note: reads the matrix the previous (needs-key) beat writes into live/matrix/. The verdict is a paired sign-flip permutation test, Holm-corrected; below --min-n (default 30) comparable pairs it reports UNDERPOWERED rather than a winner, which six samples guarantees
